conviction_note: A near non-result. The 30 Oct 2026 trading update pre-released H1 revenue (GBP134.6m, +11%, 4% organic) and said the company is on track for FY27 consensus (revenue GBP275.9m, EBITDA GBP50.8m), so the revenue line carries nothing new. The only lines left are H1 EBITDA/margin, cash, the interim dividend, the M&A pipeline and Baker Tilly rebrand costs, and none of them has a sourced bar I could beat. I sized abs_move at the European base for a pre-released period with an unchanged guide (about 3%; thin USD0.28m/day turnover offsets this name's low 0.86%/day volatility). p_up is 52 because the name's own results-day reactions skew mildly positive (6 of 7 were flat or up, including +1.5% on the identical setup last November). The findings sum to 0.0 and the scaled number is +0.12; the two do not disagree in any meaningful way.

already_public.what: H1 FY27 revenue about GBP134.6m, +11% (4% organic, 7% from the BTSEE and MS UAE acquisitions). Revenue growth, operating margins and cash conversion 'consistent with the Board's expectations'. On track for FY27 market expectations of GBP275.9m revenue and GBP50.8m underlying adjusted EBITDA. Recurring revenue about 87%.

Plan to rebrand as Baker Tilly in the UK from 1 Feb 2027 and rename the company Baker Tilly UK plc, subject to Baker Tilly International completing its purchase of the UK rights on 31 Jan 2027. Strategy and services unchanged.
FY26 results: revenue GBP251.3m, adjusted EBITDA GBP46.5m (18.5% margin), net cash GBP25.4m, total dividend 5.2p paid quarterly under a progressive policy, 'positive start to FY27'.

new_in_release.expect: H1 adjusted EBITDA and margin. Last year's H1 margin was 18.0% (GBP21.8m on GBP121.3m) against an 18.5% full year, so about 18% on GBP134.6m implies roughly GBP24m. The TU called margins 'consistent with expectations', so I expect it in line. Direction unknown.

FY27 expectations reiterated (the TU said so on 30 Oct). Hitting them needs H2 revenue of about GBP141.3m, +8.7% on H2 FY26's GBP130.0m. With MS UAE adding about 2.6 points, that implies roughly 6% organic growth, against an easier H2 FY26 comparative (about 4.3% organic, my derivation). I expect a reiteration, not a change.
Interim dividend under the progressive quarterly policy. Last year's interim was 1.0p; I expect a small increase. Priced.
Net cash after the MS UAE cash consideration (about GBP3.7m cash half). The TU called cash conversion consistent with expectations. Unknown, probably neutral.
Any cost or timetable for the Baker Tilly rebrand, M&A pipeline commentary and a possible new acquisition. Unknown.

bar: Company-stated FY27 market expectations: revenue GBP275.9m, underlying adjusted EBITDA GBP50.8m (footnote 1 of the 30 Oct 2026 RNS, https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mha-plc--mha/trading-update-and-notice-of-results-/9849158). There is no sourced H1 EBITDA bar, so any H1 margin finding would be capped small.

positioning_check: FCA aggregated register as of 2026-11-17: MHA not named, so 0.0% with no change (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv). That is the 0.5% truncation floor, not a measurement (anchor_covered false), so there is no positioning anchor and priced_lean_pct (-0.16) is essentially the run-up. Register flows: the Employee Benefit Trust rose from 9.59% (to 26 Jun 2026) to 12.17% and then to 13.11% (27 Oct 2026); Rathbones fell from 5.22% to 4.996% (28 Oct 2026). The stock rose from 130p (30 Sep) to about 144p after the TU.

findings.finding: The FY27 reiteration needs H2 revenue of about GBP141.3m (+8.7% YoY, roughly 6% organic after MS UAE) after H1 organic growth slowed to 4%, but the H2 FY26 comparative is softer (about 4.3% organic, derived from the reported FY26 6.4% and the H1 FY26 split), so the reiteration the TU already made is arithmetically plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has only ever reiterated or beaten. Reactions: Jun 2025 TU +10.1%; the May 2026 TU with EBITDA 'ahead' +3.6%; the in-line Oct 2025 TU -0.65%; in-line H1 FY26 results +1.5%.
findings.original_quote: The Group remains on track to deliver a full-year performance in line with market expectations
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. The arithmetic comes from public numbers every covering analyst has, and the company reiterated three weeks ago. If the market doubted the H2 acceleration, the stock would not have risen from 137p to 144-146p after the TU. Sized at 0 because it lands inside a guide the company has already given.
findings.independence: The comparative split comes from different documents: H1 FY26 results https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mha-plc--mha/half-year-results/9245429 and FY26 prelims https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mha-plc--mha/preliminary-results/9678485

findings.finding: The Baker Tilly UK rebrand announced 16 Nov 2026 (effective 1 Feb 2027, under licence from BTI) may come with a first statement in the interims of rebrand or licence costs, which the 16 Nov RNS does not quantify.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock moved -0.7% (145.5p to 144.5p) on the rebrand announcement day; there is no prior history.
findings.original_quote: MHA will use the name in the UK under licence from Baker Tilly International, subject to the necessary licensing arrangements being in place.
findings.why_not_priced: The licence terms and rebrand costs are not public, so the market cannot have priced a number. Rebrand costs would most likely be non-underlying, with no path to the adjusted EBITDA guide, so the finding is sized at a fraction of the money and skewed slightly negative only because no cost has been disclosed.

findings.finding: The MHA Employee Benefit Trust has kept raising its stake (9.59% to 12.17% by 26 Jun 2026, then 13.11% by 27 Oct 2026, +2.7m shares in the last step), while Rathbones dipped below 5% on 28 Oct. Net register flow ahead of the print is mildly supportive, but the EBT step may be partner-leaver transfers rather than market purchases.
findings.original_quote: Fiduchi Trustees Limited as trustee of the MHA Plc Employee Benefit Trust ... 13.113135% ... Position of previous notification 12.174455%
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. The holdings are public, and the stock's grind up from 137p to 145p in thin volume may already reflect this buyer. If the EBT were buying in the market, the 627k and 667k volume days of 23 and 27 Oct would be consistent with it. If the shares were leaver transfers, the flow says nothing. Sized small for that ambiguity.

lessons_applied: A finding on a number already told is worth 0: the guidance-arithmetic finding went from +0.1 to 0.0, because it lands inside a guide the company reiterated on 30 Oct
Understatement and thin coverage: abs_move_pct went from 2.5 to 3.0 (European base for a pre-released period with an unchanged guide, about 3%; turnover only USD0.28m/day)
The reaction history moves p_up, not size: p_up went from 53 to 52, because the mildly positive reaction skew is only weak evidence
